thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: KV cache pressure spike detected in us-east-1. p95/p99 latency breach on streaming paths. Auto-escalation -> oncall.

alex: Saw the alert. p95 jumped to 420ms (baseline 120ms), p99 ~1.2s. Streaming stalls starting at 14:03 UTC.

sam: I can take triage. Any customer-facing errors?

paul: Support: Two customers reported long hangs and 502s for chat completions starting ~14:05. Error rate ~0.8% of requests across cluster in last 10m.

maria: Traces look like heavy time in decode stage but decode workers are saturated only after prefill starts. Short summary: prefill QPS spiked on micro-shard s-42 -> KV eviction waves -> cold misses causing extra decode load -> tail latency.

alex: That matches. Pre-fill vs decode imbalance again. Do we have eviction logs?

maria: Paste from node logs: 
```
[14:06:12] shard=s-42 evict_start reason=pressure slab_free=2.1% victim_count=512
[14:06:13] shard=s-42 prefill_inflight=340 decode_active=280 kv_miss_rate=18% p99_stream=1.12s
```

sam: OK. Immediate mitigation plan options: 1) throttle prefill QPS on s-42, 2) increase slab allocation for affected shards, 3) route streaming to warm pool/standby nodes, 4) rollback recent config that increased prefill parallelism. Which is fastest?

devin: Throttle prefill is quickest. I can flip a flag to cap prefill concurrency to 75% for the shard group. Command: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/flags/pre_fill_cap -d '{"shard_group":"us-east-1-a","cap":0.75}'`

alex: Do it. Also prepare slab bump (20%) as next step if throttle doesn't stabilize p99 in 5min. sam, own validation. devin, do throttle now and share id.

devin: Throttle applied -> flag-id=ffb3c. Pre-fill concurrency capped to 75% for us-east-1-a.

maria: After throttling: p95 down to 160ms, p99 down to 420ms, kv_miss_rate dropping to 6% on s-42. Streaming stalls reduced.

paul: Customer reports improving — two accounts saw retries succeed. Marking as partial mitigation.

olivia: Any risk to throughput from throttling? We must watch backlog growth.

devin: Minimal for now. Cap only affect speculative prefill for long contexts; decode still proceeds for active requests. I'll stand by to bump slab if we see queue growth > 200/s.

sam: I'll keep tracing for tail latency patterns and check for fragmentation heatmaps. If prefill throttle works, we can avoid slab resize.

alex: Rolling handoff: I'm off in 30m. Sam will be main oncall. If this regresses, escalate to Eng-SRE paging.

sam: Ack. Running quick sanity: checking other shards for correlated pressure. Also enabling temporary routing to warm-pool nodes for streaming path for customers with active sessions.

maria: Small follow-up: found fragmentation hotspots: a bunch of small keys from an A/B test increased slot churn. Recommend reverting that test or batching keys differently.

alex: Who owns that A/B test?

tess: That's on my team. We rolled a change at 13:50 that increased ephemeral context IDs. I'll pause the rollout and revert immediately.

maria: Revert acknowledged. After revert + throttle, cluster metrics look stable: p95 ~130ms, p99 ~300ms, kv_miss_rate ~2-3%.

paul: Support: customer escalations downgraded to informational. No new 502s.

olivia: Good. Can we capture an action item list for postmortem?

alex: Action items: [1] Postmortem (sam) — root cause: prefill surge + fragmenting AB test; [2] Add circuit breaker to limit prefill vs decode ratio (devin); [3] Slab auto-resize policy review (eng-sre + eng-runtime) (maria + sam); [4] Improve hotspot detection for micro-shards (maria); [5] Revisit A/B rollout guardrails (product) (olivia + tess).

sam: I'll own the postmortem and collect traces + flamegraphs. Target draft in 24h.

devin: I'll propose immediate hardening: prefill cap flag with automated scale-down when evictions spike, and an ops runbook for this scenario.

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: mitigated -> p99 reduced to 300ms, customer error rate decreased to 0.12%. Monitoring for 1h.

alex: Thanks team. Sam takes primary oncall. handoff done.

sam: Acknowledged, monitoring. If anything changes ping @here.

paul: Closing customer-facing loop: emailing affected customers with summary and mitigation steps.

alex: Leaving note: will coordinate follow-up postmortem doc and link to graphs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT -> MONITORING -> will auto-close if stable for 60m.
